data.title: American Express Stock (AXP) Dips Over 3% on Plans to Cut 5% of Its Workforce
data.description:
American Express (AXP) stock was down 3.5% on Friday after the credit card company announced layoffs. The company plans to cut 3,500 jobs, or roughly 5% of its 78,000 workforce. This was revealed by CEO Stephen Squeri in a conference call covering the company's Q3 2026 earnings report.

According to Squeri, the layoffs are part of the company's plan to curb rising costs. He told analysts during the call that "We have got good momentum, but to accelerate innovation and win over the next few years, we needed to become a more agile and efficient organization."

American Express' decision to cut jobs comes as it tries to keep cardmembers. To achieve this, it has offered additional benefits. However, that has also increased costs at the company. In order to continue its push to keep cardmembers, layoffs were one option available as a quick way to reduce spending.

American Express noted that it suffered a charge during its third quarter related to the layoffs. The company said that it suffered a $336 million charge during the quarter as part of its restructuring. "Our strong business performance throughout the year has enabled us to step up our marketing and technology investments so we decided to use some of the gain to invest in making the organization more efficient and better prepared for the future," noted Squeri.

American Express Joins the Layoff Trend

Several companies have announced layoffs recently, including those in the financial services sector. For example, British universal bank Barclays (BCS) also announced plans to cut 5% of its workforce, or 5,000 jobs, on Thursday.

Job cuts have also been happening in other sectors this week. One example of that is e-commerce company eBay (EBAY), which said it would cut 9% of its employees, or roughly 1,000 workers, on Wednesday.

Layoffs have also been hitting tech companies as they turn to AI to reduce operating costs. Goldman Sachs (GS) estimates that roughly one in 11 workers could be displaced by AI.

Is American Express Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for American Express is Moderate Buy, based on 12 Buy, nine Hold, and one Sell rating over the past three months. With that comes an average AXP stock price target of $372.47, representing a potential 18.62% upside for the shares. Investors should expect these ratings and price targets to change following updated analyst coverage after today's earnings report. (See AXP Stock Forecast)

data.title: Gold's Price (GLD) Falls Below $4,000 to Hit Three-Month Low

The U.S. Federal Reserve is widely expected to lift interest rates another 25-basis points before the end of this year after raising them a quarter of a percentage point in September.

Higher interest rates are a negative for gold, which is a non-yielding precious ⁠metal.

data.title: Winklevoss Twins and Barry Silbert Race to Control Zcash Mining and ETFs amid 3,000% ZEC Token Surge
data.description:
Gemini Space Station (GEMI) founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss and Digital Currency Group founder Barry Silbert are pouring tens of millions of dollars into Zcash mining and exchange-traded funds as the privacy token ZEC climbs roughly 3,000%.

According to Bloomberg, the early Bitcoin (BTC-USD) buyers are using their 2012 Bitcoin strategy to buy Zcash (ZEC-USD) and build companies around the token, which lets holders hide transaction details. The two camps previously clashed during the 2022 crypto crash over the Gemini Earn program collapse.

"It's deja vu all over again with Zcash," Gemini president Cameron Winklevoss said during an October 7 talk at the Token2049 conference in Singapore. "If you had a time machine and you go back to 2013, how would you think differently and how would you operate? I think most people would say I would have bought more Bitcoin and I would have bought earlier. You now have that chance with Zcash."

U.S. Ruling Drives New Zcash Buying

Launched about 10 years ago, Zcash gained buyer attention after a March 2025 U.S. legal ruling cleared up rules around privacy coins. This decision led market figures like Arthur Hayes to pitch the token as a Bitcoin hedge. Buyers also turned to Zcash out of fear that artificial intelligence makes it easier to track money on public blockchains, alongside a rise in kidnappings and violent robberies targeting crypto holders.

"It started with a narrative as privacy became a hot topic again, well-known investors started pitching Zcash as a kind of private Bitcoin, and then real money followed," Kaiko analyst Thomas Probst told Bloomberg. Luxor Technology chief operating officer Ethan Vera noted that a "coordinated effort across a few large-scale buyers or miners, both in the U.S. and China" has since "snowballed."

Cypherpunk and Fortitude Target 20% Mining Share

The rivals now back two of the largest Zcash miners competing for a fixed token supply. Cypherpunk Technologies Inc., backed by the twins, controls about 20% of network mining power. Fortitude Mining, backed by Silbert, expects to hit 20% of mining capacity after setting up its latest machines. Both firms plan to spend tens of millions of dollars on new computing hardware.

"We believe Zcash represents one of the most compelling opportunities in digital assets," Silbert wrote in a June filing. In August, DCG's Grayscale unit launched the first U.S. Zcash ETF from a 2013 private trust. In October, the Winklevoss brothers filed for their own Zcash ETF.

At the time of writing, ZEC's token is sitting near $1,236.

data.title: SpaceX Stock Climbs Today, but 328 Million Shares Are About to Be Unlocked
data.description:
SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) is bouncing back on Friday, with shares of the space and AI giant climbing about 3% after tumbling nearly 9% on Thursday. Investors appear encouraged by news that the company is negotiating access to some 80,000 cellular towers as part of its plans to build a nationwide wireless network.

The news offers some relief after Thursday's selloff, when a broader technology slump coincided with the expiration of restrictions on 1.3 billion locked-up shares.

Yet, the rebound comes with a catch, as another lockup expiration is just around the corner. Restrictions on up to 328.4 million additional shares expire on Saturday, October 24, making those holdings eligible for trading on Monday, October 26. That could give employees and early investors another opportunity to cash out, potentially increasing the supply of SPCX stock available on the market. Of course, becoming eligible to sell doesn't necessarily mean those investors will rush to do so.

Promotion

SPCX has a long & short ETF? Explore SPCM & SPCG

SpaceX investors have already experienced seven rounds of share unlocks, and the stock hasn't followed any consistent pattern. The first release, involving 912 million shares on August 6, coincided with a 6% rally. Subsequent expirations on August 20 and September 9, each involving 319 million shares, saw SPCX fall 4% and 3.9%, respectively. A smaller release of 59 million shares on September 10 accompanied a modest 0.4% gain, while the September 24 expiration of 328 million shares saw the stock slip just 0.2%. Another tranche of the same size became available on October 9, when SPCX rose 1%.

Thursday, October 22, brought the largest single expiration yet, with 1.3 billion shares becoming eligible for sale as the stock plunged nearly 9%. However, the broader tech selloff makes it impossible to attribute that entire drop to the additional supply.

The lockup concerns come just days after SpaceX delivered quarterly results that gave investors good reasons to be encouraged. Third-quarter revenue soared 161% year over year to $14.6 billion, while net income reached $4.4 billion, compared with a $1.1 billion loss a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 306% to $8.8 billion, with the company's Super Intelligence division posting an 830% revenue increase.

Still, SpaceX isn't planning to slow its spending anytime soon, with fourth-quarter capital expenditures expected to reach $35 billion to $40 billion. Such aggressive investment could weigh on future cash flows, despite the company's strong earnings performance.

Meanwhile, SpaceX is expanding its wireless communications plans beyond its existing satellite operations. Earlier this month, it announced plans to acquire additional wireless spectrum from Grain Management, while the FCC authorized another 15,000 next-generation Starlink satellites. Combined with the latest cell tower negotiations, these developments could strengthen SpaceX's ability to compete with established telecom providers, although building a nationwide network could cost more than $80 billion.

Overall, SpaceX earns a Strong Buy consensus rating, with 29 Buys, 5 Holds, and just one Sell among 35 recent analyst recommendations. The average 12-month price target stands at $250, suggesting 68% upside from current levels. (See SPCX stock forecast)

data.title: S&P 500 Slips as Consumer Sentiment Remains at Five-Month Low
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SPX) is down by 0.16% on Friday following a consumer sentiment update from the University of Michigan. The Index of Consumer Sentiment for October came in at 48.0, above the estimate of 46.3 but down from 48.1 in September. The reading remains at its lowest level in five months as concerns over affordability and economic growth persist.

"Consumers of all political persuasions agree that inflation is overwhelmingly the greater risk to the economy in the year ahead than unemployment," said Surveys of Consumers Director Joanne Hsu.

Inflation Expectations Rise as Energy Prices Climb

Rising energy prices caused by the U.S.-Iran war have led to higher inflation expectations. Consumers now expect year-ahead inflation of 4.7%, up from 4.6% in September. That's well above the 3.4% prior to the start of the war in late February. In addition, long-term inflation expectations rose to 3.5%, up from 3.4% in the prior month. Both long-term and short-term inflation expectations are at their highest points since May.

Following a selloff on Thursday, the 10-year yield is up 4.4 basis points (bps) to 4.99% today, while the 30-year yield is up three bps to 5.31%. data.title: Dow Jones Stalls as Oil Climbs to Five-Month High
data.description:
The Dow Jones (DJIA) is down 1.13% on Friday as oil prices continue to trend higher in response to rising tensions in the Middle East. Brent crude (BZ), the global oil benchmark, is up by 1.8% to $115 per barrel, marking its highest level in five months. The U.S. continues to steadily raise its presence in the Middle East, sending additional soldiers and equipment. That comes as Iran threatens to target energy infrastructure, airports, and American bases in the region if the U.S. and Israel resume attacks, according to the Wall Street Journal.

President Trump previously said the U.S. would hold off on striking Iran before the midterm elections on November 3. However, both countries have already begun preparations for a return to action in recent days.

Hormuz Attacks Intensify as Treasury Yields Edge Higher

Iran has also increased the pace of attacks on ships traveling through the Strait of Hormuz, disrupting the global supply of energy even further. Iranian state television said that seven tankers caught fire or were damaged on Thursday night. According to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations, October has seen the highest number of reported attacks on commercial shipping in Hormuz since March, when the war was still in its early innings.

data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Gets Rare Sell Rating. Here's Why
data.description:
The stock of chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) has received a rare Sell rating. Investment firm Seaport Research slapped NVDA stock with a Sell rating, saying in a note to clients that competition is "mounting" for the company.

"We could be wrong about Nvidia in the coming months, as they leverage their supply chain heft, but competitive pressures are mounting," Seaport analyst Jay Goldberg wrote in a note to clients. "We see their aggressive finance bundling as a reaction to competitive pressure and a strategic tension at the heart of their business."

Goldberg has a $180 price target on Nvidia.

Promotion

200% short exposure to NVDA with NVDS

Delving deeper, Goldberg said he is worried that Nvidia is "over-taxing" its balance sheet, as last quarter it added roughly $250B in commitments. And while a lot of that spending has gone towards to "locking down" the supply chain, a significant portion has also gone towards supporting data center construction.

"Not included in those obligations is the $500 billion funding 'platform' Nvidia is putting together with six private equity funds and banks," Goldberg explained. "We think the company would like to make it even larger, up to $1 trillion. Nvidia will not be on the hook for all of that, but it will be a cornerstone of the whole project. The risk here is that this kind of liability is pro-cyclical. It will boost things when times are good, but when the cycle turns down, the debt will amplify the pain. At some point, probably still years away, when compute demand gets saturated, the neoclouds will put their backstops to Nvidia at just the moment when the company's cash flows get pinched by declines in sales."
data.author: Joel Baglole
